pos.personaBrief: Madrid played fast and direct (StatsBomb 1960: few patient moves, quick forward play, 69% passing) with Di Stefano driving the team, so they did not chase possession for its own sake but still attacked rather than waited.

pro.personaBrief: StatsBomb 1960 says both sides sought to get the ball quickly forward and moved faster after winning it; Di Stefano fetched balls deep and marched forward.

est.personaBrief: A W-M with a roving deep centre-forward (Spielverlagerung), Di Stefano popping up anywhere and Gento wide: fluid roles over fixed zones.

lar.personaBrief: Gento on the left supplied crosses (Puskas' header, 1960 final) and the W-M front line used wingers, though Di Stefano and Puskas centrally were the stars.

blo.personaBrief: Pressing was unstructured and the side was not good at winning the ball back (Holding Midfield, Spielverlagerung); they neither pressed in an organised way nor sat in a low block.

mar.personaBrief: StatsBomb places the era in man-marking schemes and Madrid's own scheme is unknown; the period default leans individual marking with Santamaria and Zarraga as steel.

pla.personaBrief: With seven coaches in five years the identity stayed the same: stars attacking in the same way against everyone, with the coach adapting to Di Stefano.

res.personaBrief: Winning five European Cups with a 7-3 final shot-fest: attacking spectacle in service of winning; never settling for draws or closing games.

sis.personaBrief: The side was built around Di Stefano, Puskas, Gento: talent with freedom, though Di Stefano tracked back extremely hard; a basic system did the rest.

jog.personaBrief: Technical stars (Di Stefano's ball control, Gento's pace plus technique, Kopa, Didi) with some steel in Zarraga and Santamaria; technique first.

bas.personaBrief: Bernabeu bought established stars (Di Stefano, Kopa, Puskas at 31, Didi) to win titles; no youth development emphasis.

lid.personaBrief: Stars like Di Stefano held great sway and coaches rotated constantly (Carniglia sacked partly over Puskas), so rules were not equal for all, yet Madrid had a united core.
